addendum.question: Which OpenAlex page size finishes within D122's 2.0 s source deadline, and what does a smaller page cost in anchors?
addendum.why: OpenAlex missed ASM-1a (p95 2.61 s at 50 results) and finished within 2.0 s on 18 of the spike's 30 searches. Offline, from the frozen pools: authorships is 52% of a page and select takes only whole top-level fields; dropping locations would lose the arXiv id on 183 of 1,000 records; every response was already gzip and parsing takes under 10 ms. Page size is the lever left (D125). Numbered as the second addendum; unrelated to ASM-2's allowlist A2.
addendum.queries: The 20 P1 queries: 10 topics x keyword and natural_language, each at per_page 50, 25 and 15. Every request, URL and headers, is built by the production adapter, scholiast.infrastructure.discovery.openalex.OpenAlexSource.request(text, limit=per_page): the spike's select list, with '?' and '*' replaced by spaces (D117). 60 requests.
addendum.order: Seeded with stream '<seed>/A2': the 20 queries are shuffled, and within each query the order of the three sizes is shuffled. A query's three requests run back to back.
addendum.connection: A new HTTP client, and so a new connection, for every request, as the production adapter opens one per search. Bodies are decoded as the client receives them, as in P1.
addendum.pacing: pacing['api.openalex.org']: 1 s from the previous request start, one request at a time. Retry-After and the host-stop rule apply as in pacing.
addendum.timeouts: timeouts_s.api_connect and api_total, as P1: the tail is observed, not cut at 2.0 s.
addendum.no_repeats: As rules: a failure is an outcome, and no A2 request is repeated.
addendum.measure: Per size, over all 20 requests: latency from request issued to last body byte, nearest-rank p50, p90 and p95 and the max, a failed request counted as slower than any success; the share finished within 2.0 s (Wilson); time to headers; body bytes; and the keyword-phrasing anchor recall within the page (definitions.anchor_match, using the ids P2 verified). Per query: whether the 25- and 15-result pages are, id for id and in order, the first 25 and 15 of the 50-result page. Cost from x-ratelimit-cost-usd.
addendum.decision_rule: Ship the largest per_page in {50, 25, 15} whose p95 latency is <= 2.0 s AND whose keyword-phrasing anchor recall within its own page is >= 50%. If no size passes both, none is chosen and the owner decides.
addendum.outputs: Responses to data/eval/discovery-pools-openalex-a2.json.gz with a manifest (OpenAlex data, CC0); numbers under addendum_a2 in spike/results/19_discovery_analysis.json; a section in SPIKE-FINDINGS-M4.md. The spike's committed pools are not changed.
does_not_establish: 20 requests a size make p95 the 19th-ranked value; a size that passes narrowly may not pass on another day.
One day, from the development machine's network; a deployment elsewhere sees different network latency.
The latency of a whole search: dedup and ranking (phases 7 and 8) must fit the remaining 1.0 s, and phase 10's live run measures the whole request.
Anchor recall counts 20 famous papers and is blind to precision; a smaller page may drop useful papers that are not anchors.

caveat: The pools reflect this protocol's query construction. If phase 2 changes it or the page size, the pools are re-recorded through the real adapters before any judging. Judgments attach to papers, not positions, so any already made carry over.
